label: Original-phase steps (t>=2) in sequences that open with two tokens from {f,s,r,1,j,n,h,x,z,v,3}
explanation: Fires almost only during the input phase: 97% of activation mass is there, peaking at t=3-5. It is never active at t=0 and rarely in the copy phase. It acts like an accumulator over the tokens seen so far. It is strongest when the sequence opens with tokens from a set S={f,s,r,1,j,n,h,x,z,v,3} (first_tok f gives 4.2x lift, s/r/1 about 2.5-3x; prev2_tok s/f/j about 3x). Once that prefix context exists, it fires on later new tokens. It is boosted when the current input is a first occurrence (in_first lift 1.7x) and on inputs w, o, 0 and t (w gives 3.8x). Top examples look like f n f [z v w k] and f f j [j a c h]. It is weak on repeated tokens and on prefixes without S tokens, and it decays at late positions (t>=7). It fires a little at <DEL> (2.7% of mass). The rule requiring orig(0) and orig(1) both in S plus t>=2 in the input phase reaches dev F1 0.48 (P 0.49, R 0.46, mass recall 0.58). Counting S tokens seen (>=2) with in_first gives higher recall (mass 0.79) but precision 0.27. The real behaviour looks like a graded, position-weighted sum over the history that no simple boolean rule captures.
